section: Outbreak and spread - Mangal Pandey, Meerut; centres and leaders of the revolt
subsections: Outbreak - first outbreak, Barrackpore, march to Delhi

accepted.s: Who led the defence of Delhi during the Revolt of 1857 as the real military leader, while Bahadur Shah Zafar remained the nominal leader?
accepted.x: General Bakht Khan was the real military leader at Delhi, whereas Bahadur Shah Zafar was the nominal leader.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the nominal authority from the actual military commander.

accepted.s: General Bakht Khan led which body at Delhi during the Revolt of 1857?
accepted.x: Bakht Khan led a 10-member Court of Soldiers at Delhi.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive numerical composition to identify the correct institution.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Khan Bahadur Khan led the revolt at Bareilly. Maulvi Ahmadullah was associated with Faizabad, Maulvi Liyakat Ali with Allahabad and Banaras, and Shah Mal with Baraut.
accepted.tq: Eliminate options by checking the leader against the centre of operation.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the revolt at Lucknow:
1. Begum Hazrat Mahal led the revolt.
2. She declared her son Birjis Qadr the ruler of Awadh.
3. Hindus and Muslims shared offices under the arrangement established there.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Begum Hazrat Mahal led at Lucknow, proclaimed Birjis Qadr ruler of Awadh, and the administration included both Hindus and Muslims in offices.
accepted.tq: Check whether all details associated with one centre are simultaneously correct.

accepted.s: Rani Lakshmibai was proclaimed head of state at Jhansi on:
accepted.x: Rani Lakshmibai was proclaimed head of state at Jhansi on 4 June 1858.
accepted.tq: Separate closely related dates connected with the same leader.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the revolt at Gwalior is correct?
o: It was captured by Kunwar Singh and Nana Saheb.
It was led exclusively by Bahadur Shah Zafar.
It remained under Scindia throughout the revolt.
It was captured by Lakshmibai and Tantia Tope, after which Scindia fled to Agra.
accepted.x: Rani Lakshmibai and Tantia Tope captured Gwalior, while Scindia fled to Agra.
accepted.tq: Use the leader–event–consequence chain to reject swapped associations.

accepted.s: The revolt at Bareilly was led by Khan Bahadur Khan, who proclaimed himself:
accepted.x: Khan Bahadur Khan proclaimed himself Nawab Nizam at Bareilly and commanded an army of about 40,000.
accepted.tq: Test the exact title adopted by a regional leader.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Allahabad and Banaras — Khan Bahadur Khan
accepted.x: Allahabad and Banaras were associated with Maulvi Liyakat Ali, not Khan Bahadur Khan. Khan Bahadur Khan led at Bareilly.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped leader–centre pair.

accepted.s: Shah Mal mobilised the headmen and cultivators of which area during the Revolt of 1857?
o: The chaurasee des of 84 villages in Baraut
accepted.x: Shah Mal mobilised the chaurasee des, meaning the area of 84 villages, in the Baraut region of Uttar Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Identify the distinctive local organisation and its numerical extent.

accepted.s:
Which of the following leaders and areas of operation is correctly matched?
1. Khan Bahadur Khan — Rohilkhand
2. Maulvi Ahmadullah — Faizabad
3. Kunwar Singh — Bihar
4. Tantia Tope — Central India
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four pairs are correct. Khan Bahadur Khan operated in Rohilkhand, Ahmadullah in Faizabad, Kunwar Singh in Bihar, and Tantia Tope continued guerrilla warfare in Central India.
accepted.tq: Verify each leader–region pair before selecting the coded combination.

accepted.s: Who betrayed Tantia Tope, leading to his capture and execution?
accepted.x: Tantia Tope was betrayed by Man Singh, after which he was captured and executed.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the betrayer from other figures associated with the revolt.

accepted.s: Tantia Tope continued guerrilla warfare after Nana Saheb had:
accepted.x: Nana Saheb escaped to Nepal, while Tantia Tope continued guerrilla warfare in Central India.
accepted.tq: Separate the different fates of closely associated leaders.

accepted.s: Which one of the following leaders of the Revolt of 1857 was exiled to Rangoon?
accepted.x: Bahadur Shah Zafar was exiled to Rangoon after the suppression of the revolt.
accepted.tq: Match the leader with the eventual fate rather than the area of operation.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Begum Hazrat Mahal escaped to Nepal.
2. Kunwar Singh died at Jagdishpur after being wounded.
3. Rani Lakshmibai died fighting at Gwalior.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Hazrat Mahal escaped to Nepal, Kunwar Singh died at Jagdishpur after being wounded, and Lakshmibai died fighting at Gwalior.
accepted.tq: Compare the separate post-revolt fates of regional leaders.

accepted.s: The incident involving Mangal Pandey at Barrackpore occurred on:
accepted.x: Mangal Pandey attacked British officers at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the date of the Barrackpore incident from the date of execution and the Meerut rising.
accepted.sec: Outbreak - first outbreak, Barrackpore, march to Delhi  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Mangal Pandey was hanged on 8 April 1857, and thereafter:
o: The 3rd Light Cavalry was transferred to Delhi.
The Red Fort was occupied by the rebels.
The 34th Bengal Native Infantry was disbanded.
accepted.x: Mangal Pandey was hanged on 8 April 1857 and his regiment, the 34th Bengal Native Infantry, was disbanded.
accepted.tq: Link the punishment of an individual with the administrative action against his regiment.
accepted.sec: Outbreak - first outbreak, Barrackpore, march to Delhi  [APPSC]

accepted.s: At Meerut, the immediate cause of the rising was the imprisonment of how many sepoys of the 3rd Light Cavalry for refusing the cartridges?
accepted.x: Eighty-five sepoys of the 3rd Light Cavalry were jailed for refusing the cartridges, provoking their comrades to revolt.
accepted.tq: Use the exact numerical detail to distinguish the Meerut trigger.
accepted.sec: Outbreak - first outbreak, Barrackpore, march to Delhi  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which sequence correctly represents the immediate events beginning at Meerut?
A. Sepoys broke open the jails
B. Officers were shot
C. Prisoners were freed
D. Rebels marched to Delhi
accepted.x: At Meerut, the sepoys shot their officers, broke into the jails, freed the prisoners and then marched to Delhi.
accepted.tq: Arrange the linked events by their immediate sequence rather than by date alone.
accepted.sec: Outbreak - first outbreak, Barrackpore, march to Delhi  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The slogan associated with the march of the Meerut rebels towards Delhi was:
accepted.x: The Meerut rebels marched towards Delhi shouting “Dilli Chalo”.
accepted.tq: Identify the historically associated slogan without confusing it with later nationalist slogans.
accepted.sec: Outbreak - first outbreak, Barrackpore, march to Delhi  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the events at Delhi is correct?
o: The rebels retained the existing British administration without change.
The rebels reached Delhi before the Meerut rising.
The rebels appointed Lord Canning as their emperor.
The rebels killed Commissioner Simon Fraser after entering the Red Fort.
accepted.x: After reaching Delhi, the rebels entered the Red Fort and killed Commissioner Simon Fraser. The other statements are incorrect.
accepted.tq: Reject options that reverse the sequence or wrongly assign titles and actions.
accepted.sec: Outbreak - first outbreak, Barrackpore, march to Delhi  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Lord Canning declared peace after the suppression of the revolt on:
accepted.x: Lord Canning declared peace on 8 July 1858.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year of the peace declaration from the year in which the revolt began.
accepted.sec: Outbreak - first outbreak, Barrackpore, march to Delhi  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Gwalior and Jhansi witnessed major rebel activity
B. Delhi was recaptured
C. Kanpur was retaken by Colin Campbell
D. Lucknow was recaptured
accepted.x: The sequence was Gwalior and Jhansi in June 1857, Delhi recaptured in September 1857, Kanpur retaken in December 1857, and Lucknow recaptured in March 1858.
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence using the month in which each centre was recaptured or occupied.
accepted.sec: Outbreak - first outbreak, Barrackpore, march to Delhi  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following centres was recaptured by the British in September 1857?
accepted.x: Delhi was recaptured in September 1857. Kanpur was retaken in December 1857, Lucknow in March 1858 and Bareilly in May 1858.
accepted.tq: Match each centre with its month of recapture.
accepted.sec: Outbreak - first outbreak, Barrackpore, march to Delhi  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Colin Campbell retook which centre in December 1857?
accepted.x: Colin Campbell retook Kanpur in December 1857.
accepted.tq: Identify the military commander associated with the recapture of a centre.
accepted.sec: Outbreak - first outbreak, Barrackpore, march to Delhi  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about the spread and suppression of the revolt is correct?
1. Jhansi was recaptured in April 1858.
2. Kunwar Singh led a fresh rising in Bihar in April 1858.
3. Bareilly was recaptured in May 1858.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Jhansi was recaptured and Kunwar Singh led a fresh rising in Bihar in April 1858, while Bareilly was recaptured in May 1858.
accepted.tq: Combine several late-stage developments and verify their months independently.
accepted.sec: Outbreak - first outbreak, Barrackpore, march to Delhi  [APPSC]
